headline: After an 11% run in two weeks, the night brought worse news: higher US bond rates, higher oil and Indian inflation above 6%. Expect a softer start and a pause, with foreign buying still supporting the trend.

mood.label: Mixed
mood.why: Dashboard +29 (mildly bullish) but only 2 of 4 checks agree, and overnight news leans negative. Overnight data as of 08:47 IST.

key_points.text: Since India closed, the US 10-year bond rate rose to **5.13%** and Brent oil rose 3.5%. Both usually hurt Indian stocks.
India's October inflation, out after the close, was **6.09%**, above the RBI's 6% limit. An RBI rate rise on 4 December is now more likely.
Foreign investors (FIIs) bought **₹7,831 crore** of Indian shares yesterday, their third big buying day in a row.
My call: a lower start and a pause inside **25,000-25,500**, not a reversal. Low confidence.

sections.title: What changed overnight
sections.summary: Mostly worse news for the open, working against the rally.

points.text: GIFT Nifty (overnight Nifty futures) was around **25,200-25,240**, 60-100 points below Nifty's 25,299 close. Sources differ slightly.
US stocks fell about 0.4%, hit by reports of a leadership shake-up at Nvidia (I couldn't confirm details). US futures are now up 0.3%, and Japan and Taiwan are up 1.6-2%.
The US 10-year bond rate rose **0.13 points** to 5.13%. Higher safe US returns tend to pull foreign money out of India.
Brent oil rose **3.5%** since India closed, to $95.5, which hurts an oil importer like India. US-listed HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank fell about 1%.

sections.title: Bounce or continuation?
sections.summary: A soft start and a sideways day, uptrend intact. Low confidence.

points.text: Signs of a pause: Nifty is up **11.5%** since 28 October, its highest since February, but gained only 0.18% yesterday. Domestic funds sold ₹6,331 crore.
Signs it can continue: FIIs bought 1.7 times their normal daily amount. Their share of index-futures bets on a rise jumped from 10.6% to **37%** in nine sessions, with room to go higher.
Overnight news is worse: higher US rates, oil and Indian inflation. That argues against a strong push higher today.
What would prove me wrong: a close above **25,500** means the run is continuing. A close below 25,000, or FIIs turning sellers, would mean a deeper pullback.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.summary: Leans bullish at +29, but the checks disagree.

points.text: Price trend (+1): Nifty is well above its 20, 50 and 200-day averages (all below 24,000).
Futures (+2, the maximum): price rose and open bets in Nifty futures grew **6%**. New money is betting on a rise.
Option chain (-0.7): sellers added many calls at 25,300 (bets Nifty stays below it), building a ceiling. The 25,000 floor also grew.
Put-call ratio (bets on a fall vs bets on a rise) is a normal **1.00**. India VIX (expected swings) is 16.6, higher than 75% of last year, so expect bigger moves.

sections.title: What big investors are doing
sections.summary: Foreigners buy hard; domestic funds take profits.

points.text: FIIs bought **₹73,566 crore** this month. Analysts link it to money leaving AI-heavy markets like the US and Taiwan, plus cheaper oil.
FIIs cut net bets on a fall by **20,700** index-futures contracts yesterday, which means buying.
FIIs are still about ₹2.41 lakh crore net sellers for 2026, so their mood can turn fast if US rates keep rising. Domestic funds sold ₹46,835 crore this month.

sections.title: What the world is telling India
sections.summary: A helpful month, but US rates turned against India this week.

points.text: The dashboard's one-month view says the world is mostly helping India: oil is about 10% cheaper and the rupee 1% stronger.
But the US 10-year rate rose **0.29 points** this week, a red flag on the dashboard. The dollar is up 1.6%.
Markets now expect the US Fed to **raise** rates in December after hotter US inflation.

sections.title: Company results
sections.summary: No Nifty 50 company reported, so results are a side story.

points.text: Manappuram Finance: profit up **223%** vs last year, revenue up 47%.
NMDC: revenue up 4%, profit down 1.8%, roughly flat.
Reliance Power profit fell 66%; Amber Enterprises made a loss. I couldn't confirm analyst expectations for these.

sections.title: What could change the picture
sections.summary: Interest rates in India and the US are the big theme.

points.text: Tonight 7 pm IST: US producer prices. A hot number pushes US rates up. Expiries on 17 and 23 November can bring sharp swings.
4 December: RBI decision. With inflation at 6.09%, a rate rise is possible.
10 December (IST): US Fed decision. A bigger-than-expected hike would hurt.

levels.note: A close above 25,500 would mean option sellers lost their ceiling and the rally is extending. A close below 25,000 would break the floor and point to a deeper pullback.

watch.text: Pre-open: does Nifty open near 25,200, and do FIIs buy the dip?
Banks and lenders after the 6.09% inflation number.
US producer prices. A hot reading lifts US rates.
Evening FII data: a fourth big buying day supports the trend.

bottom_line: The dashboard leans bullish (+29) because foreign funds are buying, but only 2 of 4 checks agree, so confidence is low. Overnight news is mostly negative: US rates and oil rose, and Indian inflation crossed 6%. My read is a softer start and a sideways day between 25,000 and 25,500, not the end of the uptrend. The main risk is rising US rates turning foreign buyers into sellers; a close below 25,000 would be the first sign.
